nature.note: Article pages were reachable but no independent Graphical Abstract/Visual Abstract/TOC semantic marker was found; existing Figure fallbacks remain correctly classified.

evidence.result: publisher article is crawlable through the native web index and explicitly contains a Graphical Abstract section, but the extraction surface did not expose the Graphical Abstract image src; therefore no unsafe image substitution was written.

an early isolated browser fetch reached the ACS Silverchair abstract page and exposed an article CDN image, but the later full 87-DOI pass was bot-blocked for all ACS targets. The isolated image was not promoted because strong TOC semantics could not be bound to it.

infrastructureIssue.workerMediaInventory: Cloudflare Worker 1101 / HTTP 500 during the full queue seed
infrastructureIssue.effect: The GPT pass was forced to reconstruct the 168-gap universe from the deployed GitHub Pages artifact/media-index rather than the live media inventory. This did not change the attempted DOI set, but prevented normal write-back/queue verification.

conclusion: Full direct GPT publisher-page crawling was attempted for all 168 current non-official-TOC gaps. No new image met the project's strong official-TOC evidence threshold. This is a negative but useful production test: GPT web access is good for semantic verification and Wiley index discovery, but bulk image acquisition for ACS/Wiley/Science still requires an authenticated/local-browser/VPN-capable media collector or a source that exposes the raw image URL.
